fullName: RRB ALP and Technician (Assistant Loco Pilot, Technician Grade I Signal and Technician Grade III)
overview: This is Indian Railways' recruitment for its **running and maintenance staff**: **Assistant Loco Pilot (ALP)** in the loco cabin, and **Technicians** who keep locos, coaches, signalling and workshop equipment running. The Railway Recruitment Boards fill these posts through two parallel notifications in each cycle: a **CEN for ALP** and a **CEN for Technician Grade I Signal and Grade III**. The ALP path is a two-stage exam: **CBT 1 (screening) → CBT 2 with Part A (merit) and Part B (trade, qualifying) → Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) → document verification → medical**. The Technician path is shorter: a **single CBT**, then DV and medical, with a separate CBT for each pay level. There is no interview at any stage. What makes this exam different from NTPC or SSC papers is the **technical core**: General Science at 10th standard level for the CBTs, and for ALP a full **Basic Science and Engineering** paper plus a trade test in CBT 2. Fitness matters as much as marks: ALP needs **A-1 medical standard** (6/6 vision without glasses, no LASIK surgery), so read the medical annexure before you commit.

Age is counted as on **1 July 2026**. Apply only through the official RRB websites and the rrbapply.gov.in portal; beware of fake sites. stages.name: CBT 1: First Stage (ALP) / single CBT (Technician)
stages.nature: ALP: screening for CBT 2 · Technician: merit-deciding
stages.notes: **ALP CBT 1 (CEN 01/2026): 75 questions, 75 marks, 60 minutes**, negative marking 1/3, marks normalised across shifts. The CEN lists three subject areas: **Mathematics, Mental Ability and General Science (10th standard Physics, Chemistry and Life Sciences)**. The 2026 CEN does **not** fix a section-wise question count and has **no separate General Awareness or current affairs area** (the 2025 CEN still had one), so treat the whole paper as the three areas above. Minimum qualifying marks: **UR and EWS 40%, OBC-NCL and SC 30%, ST 25%**. CBT 1 marks do **not** count in the final panel. **Technician CBT (CEN 02/2026) is a different paper: 100 questions, 90 minutes**, one CBT per pay level. Tentative break-up from the CEN: **Grade III** has Mathematics 25, General Intelligence and Reasoning 25, General Science 40, General Awareness 10; **Grade I Signal** has General Awareness 10, Reasoning 15, Basics of Computers and Applications 20, Mathematics 20, Basic Science and Engineering 35. The CEN calls these break-ups indicative.

stages.name: CBT 2: Second Stage, Part A (merit) + Part B (trade test)
stages.nature: Part A: merit-deciding · Part B: qualifying
stages.notes: **ALP only. One combined sitting: Part A of 100 questions in 90 minutes plus Part B of 75 questions in 60 minutes (175 questions, 150 minutes in total).** Part A covers Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning and **Basic Science and Engineering** (engineering drawing, units and measurements, work power and energy, heat and temperature, basic electricity, levers and simple machines, safety, environment, IT literacy). Only **Part A marks count** for shortlisting to CBAT, and only if you also score the **35% qualifying marks in Part B (for every category)**. Part B questions come from your **ITI trade syllabus as prescribed by DGT**; ITI and Act Apprentice candidates get their own trade, while diploma and degree holders choose one trade from the grouping table in the CEN (electrical, electronics, mechanical or automobile streams). Minimum qualifying in Part A: UR and EWS 40%, OBC-NCL and SC 30%, ST 25%.

stages.name: Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
stages.nature: Qualifying, with 50% weight in the final merit
stages.notes: **ALP only.** Candidates equal to **8 times** the ALP vacancies for each community are shortlisted for CBAT on the basis of Part A of CBT 2, after qualifying in Part B. The CBAT runs **only in English and Hindi**, has **no negative marking**, and is split into test batteries; you must **clear every battery separately** with a minimum **T-score of 42 in each**, with no relaxation for any category. From CEN 01/2026 the final merit is built as **50% Part A of CBT 2 + 50% CBAT** (the 2025 CEN used 70:30, so always recheck the ratio in the notice you apply under). Candidates must carry the **Self-Screening Medical Declaration Report** (Annexures VIII A and VIII B), signed by a general physician and an eye specialist from a government hospital or medical college, on CBAT day. Practice material is published by RDSO on its Psychology Candidate's Corner page.

stages.name: Document Verification and Medical Examination
stages.notes: For ALP, the DV shortlist is drawn from candidates who qualify in the CBAT, in the ratio of the vacancies; ties are broken first by **age (older candidate ranks higher)** and then alphabetically. For Technician, candidates equal to the vacancies are shortlisted for DV directly on CBT merit. Before your DV date you must upload scanned copies (in true colour) of your photo and signature on the **orims-ir.gov.in/rbdv** portal. At DV you produce all original certificates; absence or failure to produce originals forfeits the candidature. Appointment depends on clearing the railway **medical examination**: **A-1 for ALP** (distant vision 6/6, 6/6 without glasses, colour, binocular, night and mesopic vision tests; no LASIK), and **B-1, A-3, B-2 or C-1 for Technician posts** as per the post parameters annexure. A one-time medical appeal with prescribed charges is allowed if you fail the initial medical.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India, or a citizen of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 to settle permanently, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka and the East African countries listed in the notice, with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India where required.

education.requirement: **Matriculation/SSLC (10th pass) plus ITI** in the notified trades (Fitter, Electrician, Instrument Mechanic, Millwright/Maintenance Mechanic, Mechanic Radio and TV, Electronics Mechanic, Mechanic Motor Vehicle, Wireman, Tractor Mechanic, Armature and Coil Winder, Mechanic Diesel, Heat Engine, Turner, Machinist, Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Mechanic) from NCVT/SCVT institutions, **or** 10th plus a Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in those trades, **or** 10th plus a **three-year Diploma** in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics or Automobile Engineering (or a combination of streams) in lieu of ITI. A degree in the same disciplines is also accepted in lieu of the diploma.

**B.Sc** in Physics, Electronics, Computer Science, Information Technology or Instrumentation (or a combination of these basic streams), **or a three-year Diploma in Engineering** in these streams, **or an Engineering degree** in the same disciplines. There is no ITI route for this post.

**10th pass plus ITI** (NCVT/SCVT) in the trade given against each post category, **or 10th plus Course Completed Act Apprenticeship (CCAA)** in that trade. Diploma and degree holders should note the CEN's rule that an engineering **diploma or degree is not accepted in lieu of ITI/CCAA** for Level 2 Technician posts unless a post specifically says so.

eligibility.notes: Qualifications must be **in hand on or before the closing date** of the CEN; candidates awaiting results cannot apply. PwBD candidates are **not eligible for ALP** in CEN 01/2026, and Technician posts accept PwBD only in the categories marked in the post parameters annexure. LASIK or any other refractive surgery makes you ineligible for posts with **A-1 and A-3** standards. Age relaxations are **not cumulative**; if eligible on more than one ground you get the maximum of them, and SC, ST and OBC candidates applying against UR vacancies get no relaxation. The detailed CEN of the cycle you apply in is the final word.

selectionProcess: **ALP (CEN 01/2026): CBT 1 (screening) → CBT 2 Part A (merit) + Part B (trade, 35% qualifying) → CBAT (T-score 42 in every battery) → Document Verification → Medical Examination.** The final merit is **50% Part A of CBT 2 + 50% CBAT**; CBT 1 marks are not counted. **Technician (CEN 02/2026): a single CBT per pay level → Document Verification → Medical Examination**, with the DV shortlist prepared RRB-wise at 1:1 on normalised CBT marks. There is **no interview and no typing or skill test** in either path. Vacancies, post preference and medical standard together decide the final allotment of the railway zone and post.
normalization: Both CBTs are held over multiple days and shifts with different question papers, so raw scores are **normalised across shifts** before results, using the RRBs' published normalisation method. Only the normalised score decides shortlisting and merit. In practice: never compare raw marks with friends in other shifts; a shift with a tougher paper is statistically adjusted in your favour; and a raw score just below a cutoff you have heard of may still clear after normalisation, so wait for the official result rather than assuming.

faqs.q: Is there negative marking in the RRB ALP and Technician exams?
faqs.a: Yes. **1/3 mark is deducted for every wrong answer** in every CBT, whether ALP CBT 1, ALP CBT 2 or the Technician CBT. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and unattempted questions cost nothing. The **CBAT has no negative marking**.

faqs.q: What is the ALP CBT 1 pattern?
faqs.a: **75 questions for 75 marks in 60 minutes**, all objective, with 1/3 negative marking. The 2026 CEN lists the subject areas as **Mathematics, Mental Ability (General Intelligence and Reasoning) and General Science** of 10th standard level. The CEN does **not publish a fixed section-wise question count** for CBT 1, and the separate General Awareness area that existed in the 2025 CEN has been dropped, so prepare the three areas and expect any reasonable spread across them.

It is one sitting of **2 hours 30 minutes with 175 questions**. **Part A: 100 questions in 90 minutes** covering Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning and **Basic Science and Engineering**; only Part A marks count for merit. **Part B: 75 questions in 60 minutes** from your **ITI trade syllabus (DGT)**; it is only qualifying, but you must score **at least 35%** in it irrespective of category, or Part A marks do not help you.

faqs.q: What is the CBAT and how much does it count in the merit?
faqs.a: The Computer Based Aptitude Test is a psychometric test for **ALP candidates only**, held after CBT 2. Candidates equal to **8 times the vacancies** per community are called. It runs in English and Hindi, has no negative marking, and you need a **T-score of at least 42 in each test battery**, with no relaxation. In the 2026 CEN the final merit is **50% Part A of CBT 2 + 50% CBAT**; the 2025 CEN used 70:30, so always confirm the ratio in the notice you applied under.

faqs.q: What is the qualification for ALP and Technician posts?
faqs.a: **ALP:** 10th pass **plus ITI** in a notified trade, or 10th plus a Course Completed Act Apprenticeship, or 10th plus a **three-year engineering diploma** (degree also accepted in lieu of diploma). **Technician Grade III:** 10th plus ITI/CCAA in the post's trade, and a diploma is **not** accepted in lieu of ITI for these Level 2 posts. **Technician Grade I Signal:** B.Sc, or a three-year engineering diploma, or an engineering degree in the notified streams; there is no ITI route. Qualifications must be complete before the application closing date.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for this recruitment?
faqs.a: For the 2026 cycle, age is counted as on **1 July 2026**: **18 to 30 years** for ALP and Technician Grade III, and **18 to 33 years** for Technician Grade I Signal. Standard relaxations apply: OBC-NCL +3 years, SC/ST +5 years, and separate limits for ex-servicemen, serving railway staff, widowed or divorced women and Act Apprentices as given in the CEN table.

faqs.q: What is the application fee and how does the refund work?
faqs.a: **₹500** for all other candidates, of which **₹400 is refunded after you appear in the first CBT**; **₹250** for SC, ST, ex-servicemen, female, transgender, minority and EBC candidates, **fully refunded after you appear**. The refund is credited only to an **Aadhaar-seeded bank account** that you validate during the application. For Technician, the fee is payable **separately for each pay level**, since each level has its own CBT.

faqs.q: How do the ALP and Technician selections differ?
faqs.a: **ALP** has two CBTs: CBT 1 screens, CBT 2 decides merit through Part A, and the CBAT adds an aptitude gate with a 50% weight. **Technician** has a **single CBT** (100 questions, 90 minutes) whose normalised marks directly build the DV shortlist at 1:1 of vacancies; Grade I Signal aspirants additionally face a **Basics of Computers and Applications** block in the paper. Both paths end with document verification and a railway medical, and neither has an interview.

faqs.q: Can I choose my exam language?
faqs.a: For the CBTs, questions appear in **English, Hindi and 13 regional languages** (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu); you pick one medium in the application and it cannot be changed. The **CBAT is conducted only in English and Hindi**.

faqs.q: What are the medical standards and why do they matter so much here?
faqs.a: ALP demands the **A-1 standard**: distant vision 6/6, 6/6 **without glasses**, near vision without glasses, and passing tests for colour, binocular, field, night and mesopic vision. Candidates who have had **LASIK or similar refractive surgery are not eligible**, and a self-screening medical declaration with certificates signed by a government doctor must be produced on CBAT day. Technician posts require B-1, A-3, B-2 or C-1 depending on the trade. Failing the medical means no appointment on that post and no alternative post, so check your fitness before investing a year of preparation.

documents: Keep these ready for the application and for **Document Verification**: **Class 10 (matriculation) certificate** as date of birth and qualification proof, **ITI/NTC/NAC or Act Apprenticeship certificates** in the relevant trade (or diploma and degree certificates, with all semester marksheets), **category certificate** in the central format (OBC-NCL issued after 1 April 2026 where applicable, EWS, SC or ST), **EBC income certificate, BPL card or Izzat MST** if you claimed the fee concession, **ex-servicemen documents** where applicable, a **valid photo ID** (Aadhaar preferred, since fee refunds need an Aadhaar-seeded bank account), a **colour passport photograph not older than two months** for the exam and DV, and your scanned **signature in running handwriting** (JPG, 30 to 49 KB). The application itself captures a **live photograph** through your webcam or phone camera, so dress in dark clothing against a plain background. Before DV, photo and signature scans must be uploaded on the orims-ir.gov.in/rbdv portal. SC and ST candidates who opt for the **free sleeper-class train pass** must upload their caste certificate with the application and carry the original at every stage. Any mismatch in name or date of birth across documents is the commonest cause of DV trouble, so fix it with a gazette notification before you apply.

calendar.note: Dates are taken from the detailed CEN 01/2026 and CEN 02/2026 and the exam schedule notices issued on the official RRB websites in September 2026. CBT dates can shift for administrative reasons, and your e-call letter is the final word on your date, shift and centre. Always confirm on the official RRB portals.
